sentence: Sending a bed_id or watering id above 64 bits (e.g. 99999999999999999999) to POST/GET/DELETE /api/waterings returns a 500 Internal Server Error instead of a 4xx.
evidence: Signed in via POST /api/auth/login as the demo user, then used curl against the running API. POST /api/waterings {"bed_id":99999999999999999999,"litres":1} -> 500 'Internal Server Error'; GET /api/waterings?bed_id=99999999999999999999 -> 500; DELETE /api/waterings/99999999999999999999 -> 500; POST with bed_id 9223372036854775808 (2^63) -> 500. For comparison, in-range bed_id 999999 -> 422 {"detail":"Choose an existing bed."} and GET ?bed_id=999999 -> 200 []. Code: WateringIn.bed_id is Field(gt=0) and the query/path params are plain int with no upper bound, so Python ints above the 64-bit limit reach sqlite3, which raises OverflowError, and nothing handles it. Only the API is affected; the UI never sends such ids.
